newsitem.title: USA: Gene-altered corn could be next protest target.
newsitem.headline: Gene-altered corn could be next protest target.

text.p: Genetically-altered corn may be the next target in an ongoing battle between U.S. producers and environmental groups.

But U.S. trade groups on Friday affirmed their stance that Bt corn, a genetic strain modified to resist the European corn borer crop pest, does not require special labelling and should not be separated from other corn.
"When it comes to labelling, I think we would be adamantly opposed to such a move," said Mike Orso, spokesman for the National Corn Growers Association.
Bt corn seed is produced from corn modified by inserting specific genes from the common soil bacterium bacillus thuringiensis (Bt).
Swiss chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Ciba-Geigy AG, which makes Bt corn, said Thursday it was awaiting a decision by European Union officials on its application to import and plant Bt corn.

But with that approval could come protests by environmental groups that have pushed for boycotts against genetically altered "Roundup Ready" soybeans and asked that products made from the crops be labelled.
The corn is sold as Maximizer by Ciba Seeds and NatureGard by Mycogen Corp.
Greenpeace activists this week staged protests in Antwerp and Hamburg to coincide with the arrival of ships they believed contained genetically altered soybeans.
Approximately 600,000 acres of Bt corn was planted this year in the United States, or about 0.75 percent of the planted crop, according to the U.S. Corn Refiners Association.
In a September 24 statement, the association said separating genetically altered corn and labelling products made from the corn was unnecessary and costly.
"While there are limited systems for segregation and identity-preservation of grain with specific performance characteristics, such sytems are extremely limited and costly," the association said.

"It is the policy of the Corn Refiners Association that no statutory, regulatory, compositional, environmental, food or feed-safety issues exist to prevent the utilization of Bt corn, as approved by the U.S. government, in the corn wet milling industry," the association said.

Biotechnology foes last month announced a worldwide boycott of genetically-altered corn and soybeans, asking consumers to stay away from such products as McDonald's Corp french fries and Coca-Cola Co products.
European trade group EuroCommerce has asked for labelling of transgenic corn and soybeans.
Some canola and cotton is also grown from genetically altered seeds.
